key_insight: Suvorexant increased the phosphorylated-to-unphosphorylated tau-181 ratio in plasma while decreasing it in cerebrospinal fluid, revealing opposite biomarker responses across compartments.
clinical_relevance: Medication-related shifts in plasma tau biomarkers may complicate interpretation in Alzheimer disease screening and trial enrollment; this study did not examine AI or cancer drug discovery.
method: Secondary analysis of a randomized, placebo-controlled trial involving 25 participants receiving placebo or suvorexant 20 mg.
Longitudinal paired cerebrospinal fluid and plasma sampling, with plasma Alzheimer biomarkers measured by mass spectrometry.
SomaScan 11K proteomic profiling at hours 0, 16, and 24.
evidence_signal: Between 08:00 and 16:00, tau-181 phosphorylation ratios shifted in opposite directions in plasma and cerebrospinal fluid, alongside compartment- and time-dependent proteomic changes.
watch_item: This small, acute secondary analysis does not establish long-term biomarker effects or clinical benefit in Alzheimer disease.
paper_title: Suvorexant Inversely Affects Phosphorylated Tau in Human Cerebrospinal Fluid and Plasma
